newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich, Lott invite Clinton for a talk.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich, Lott invite Clinton for a talk.

text.p: The two top Republicans in Congress invited President Clinton Monday for talks on major issues facing the country on the morning after his Tuesday State of the Union address.
But Clinton will be unable to take up the invitation extended by Senate Leader Trent Lott and House Speaker Newt Gingrich because he will be travelling to Gingrich's home state of Georgia.
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry said aides for Clinton would contact the congressional leaders to set a time for talks. "I assume he will take them up on their offer to meet," McCurry said.

The two Republican leaders, citing "much talk of bipartisanship" in the last few weeks, said in a letter to Clinton they believed Republicans and Democrats could find common ground for action in five areas.
They were: balancing the federal budget by the year 2002; tax relief and jobs; improving education; confronting the problem of crime and drugs and addressing the problems of toxic and nuclear waste.
"We believe there is enough common ground to find reasonable solutions to these problems this year," Lott and Gingrich said.
"We hope that you and the bipartisan leadership in the House and Senate will be able to meet with us this Wednesday to begin discussions on this common agenda for the American people."
